# Matrix Watcher

> https://matrixwatcher.space is a public observation experiment. It publishes source coverage and timing controls alongside unusual events. No cross-domain discovery or predictive signal has been independently validated.

## Current system

- The live configuration monitors 16 sources: 11 anomaly-eligible streams, one locally calculated earth-tide covariate and four context feeds. Sources that share a physical domain or API are not independent tests.
- The context feeds are delayed NASA fireball reports, paired RIPE Atlas K-root/F-root probes, six-city Open-Meteo model estimates and physical airport METAR reports from New York, Riga, São Paulo, Cape Town, Tokyo and Sydney. Context feeds never add anomaly-cluster votes. Model estimates, station temperatures and airport altimeter settings are different measurements.
- An unavailable or partial source is a coverage issue. ANU hardware samples are required for the quantum stream; other entropy is never labelled quantum. Wikipedia history replay is bounded and exposes gaps.
- Live clusters count distinct domains within 30 seconds. A cluster level is a descriptive coincidence count, not a p-value or proof of causation.

## Research status

- Evidence Lab compares 30-second, 5-minute and 15-minute three-domain episodes with within-month shifted-time controls. Historical results are exploratory.
- Observation Atlas estimates sampling opportunity for selectable 30-second, 5-minute, 15-minute and 1-hour hypothetical event durations, not detector power or joint-source availability. Lag Lab tests twelve predefined source/lag comparisons with a timing control and multiple-comparison correction.
- A 120-day future-data lag screen and a five-rule Forecast Audit run from 2026-09-24 to 2027-01-22 UTC. The forecast diary scores binary outcomes only when target coverage is adequate. No rule is automatically promoted to a validated public signal.
- A separate observation-time coincidence screen is frozen for 2026-09-25 to 2027-01-23 UTC. New anomaly records keep distinct source-event, publication, observation and detection clocks where available; absent upstream times remain null. Three windows are tested only at the endpoint, with whole missing days excluded from the timing control. Day-level coverage matching cannot remove within-day outages or reporting delays. This is an exploratory screen, not an automatic discovery.
- Historical collection and processing gaps remain in the archive despite repaired code. A quiet dashboard cannot, by itself, rule out a short or delayed event.
